A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLaRe study. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments comparing three neural architectures and four training objectives on 18 formal languages, plus error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds model-size experiments and analyses of performance by input length.

M1.justification: The architectures, objectives and sampling strategy remain the same. Algorithm 3, line 8, corrects backward-weight aggregation from a semiring product over destination states to a sum. This changes the documented algorithm locally, without establishing an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 18 formal languages and recognition tasks. The new size experiments and length-dependent analyses use retained coverage; they introduce no new language, domain or input-length range.

E2.justification: The evaluated architectures remain the simple RNN, LSTM and causally masked transformer, with the same four objectives in the main experiments. MLRegTest and Weiss et al. receive expanded discussion but are not added as empirical comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds controlled experiments at approximately 32k, 64k and 128k parameters using recognition-only training under the expressivity setup. Appendix I introduces cross-entropy aggregation within overlapping length windows. The original training, validation and test protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix H tests whether model size explains failures across 16 languages, while Appendix I examines length-dependent losses across all 18 languages. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's retained auxiliary-objective comparisons, error inspection and edit-distance analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix I newly reports one-standard-deviation bands around cross-entropy means within length windows. The standard deviations added to main Table 2 were already available in v1's detailed tables, and the existing ten-run reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 22 and Figure 3 add substantial size-dependent and length-dependent results. For example, recognition-only transformer accuracy on Modular Arithmetic is 0.86, 0.83 and 0.92 at 32k, 64k and 128k parameters. These are new experimental comparisons, not same-setting improvements over Table 2. All original Table 2 central values and Tables 4–21 remain unchanged; the Bucket Sort narrative correctly replaces RNN with LSTM.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the purported probability semiring on [0,1] with the nonnegative real semiring, adds tightness to the PDFA definition and corrects backward aggregation. Runtime bounds now account for transitions and sampling's logarithmic out-degree factor; Appendix F derives MLRegTest's complexity. These refine the existing mathematics; the edit-distance theorem and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The recognition framework, FLaRe benchmark and architecture/objective conclusions remain central. The abstract and conclusion drop the broad claim of much better complexity than previous methods, instead claiming an efficient algorithm. The introduction additionally emphasizes the tested architectures' empirical restriction to low Chomsky-hierarchy levels.

C2.justification: v2 adds an applicability limitation for rejection sampling when a language's complement is small and qualifies Repeat 01's sensitivity as distribution-dependent. It also uses the new analyses to suggest architectural rather than size limitations and to distinguish recognition generalization from transduction findings. These substantially expand the explanation and boundaries of the results.

D1.justification: v2 makes NEXT an explicit input to Algorithm 7, corrects intermediate vector dimensions and explains the binary-search behavior of the sampling implementation. Neural-head parameter dimensions are clearer. Existing code/data access information, CPU execution and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: New Section 3.4 and Appendix F substantially develop the comparison with MLRegTest and Weiss et al., distinguishing language coverage, complement handling, sampling distributions, edit limits and runtime. This qualifies the sampling-efficiency positioning. Additional foundational and tightness references also expand the context beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and reorganizes the exposition into separate Background and Method sections. Dataset generation is divided into positive sampling, efficient sampling and negative sampling; detailed explanations move into a reorganized Appendix B. Terminology changes from counting to binning semiring, and a dedicated prior-work comparison is added.

P2.justification: v2 adds the hierarchy summary diagram, the 18-panel length-performance figure and the model-size table. Table 2 gains displayed standard deviations and bold best scores, Table 3 moves to the appendix, and the retained edit-distance plot is restyled. These substantially change the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the existing study through mathematical and pseudocode corrections, more explicit comparison with MLRegTest, and clearer sampling limitations. The size controls and length-dependent plots strengthen interpretation of the retained results. These are useful, bounded improvements in rigor and explanatory support; the principal benchmark evidence and conclusions remain stable.
